subject: Pricing annex: harmonization of fee bands & cap-floor language
messages:
From: Emma Jones <emma.jones@polarishealth.com>
To: sofia_ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@polarishealth.com
Date: 2027-01-17T09:12:00-05:00
Subject: Pricing annex: harmonization ask for fee bands and caps

Hi Sofia / Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our procurement team reviewed the order form and the attached pricing annex and came back with a marked-up redline (attached). The key asks are:

- Harmonize the fee bands so our multiple business units see the same anchoring (they cited ambiguity around how slab thresholds apply across SKUs).
- Clarify the interaction between the fee floor (minimum monthly commitment) and the cap (true-up protections) — they are worried the current language could double-count credits during scaled-down months.
- Add a short carveout that allows an emergency rollback for capped usage in the event of unplanned outages (internal ops requirement).

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept the harmonization approach or propose alternative language we could take to our legal team? We need a working draft by end-of-week to keep our board timeline.

I've attached Polaris_Redline_Annex.docx with inline comments. Happy to jump on a short call if that's easier.

Best,
Emma Jones
Sr. Procurement Manager, Polaris Health
emma.jones@polarishealth.com
Polaris Health — Procurement

Attachment: Polaris_Redline_Annex.docx (redline with inline comments)

From: sofia_ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@polarishealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-01-17T12:30:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Pricing annex: harmonization ask for fee bands and caps

Emma — thanks for the clear summary and for the redline. I've read the comments and pulled together a short summary of implications for both pricing and ops (attached). High-level:

- Harmonizing fee bands: operationally straightforward but will reduce near-term revenue visibility unless we preserve SKU-level multipliers. We can propose "harmonized bands + SKU multipliers" language to keep predictability.

- Cap/floor interaction: Polaris' redline attempts to prevent double-crediting; that's reasonable. We need to ensure the true-up calculation is explicitly sequential (apply floor, then cap/credits) in the annex so there's no ambiguity.

- Emergency rollback carveout: acceptable with a 30-day notice and mutual confirmation clause. We should limit it to outages attributable to infrastructure events (force majeure/backplane failure) and exclude customer-side outages.

Action items I propose:
1) Karthik — please draft concrete annex language (short snippet) that implements sequential true-up math and the harmonized-band approach.
2) Ben — confirm commercial concession range we can offer for harmonization (one-time credit vs. permanent band change).
3) Laura — check with legal on whether the rollback carveout language will create any open indemnity or audit obligations.

I've attached Sofia_Summary.pdf (2p) with bullet callouts. If agreeable, we can turn Karthik's language into a tracked-change doc to return to you by tomorrow EOD.

— Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Head of Account Strategy, Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com

Attachment: Sofia_Summary.pdf

From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: sofia_ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-01-18T08:45:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Pricing annex: harmonization ask for fee bands and caps

Folks — following Sofia's notes, here's a compact proposal we can send back to Polaris. I'm attaching a tracked-change annex (proposed_annex_markup.docx) but include the key snippet inline below for speed.

PROPOSED SNIPPET (for Annex A — Pricing Mechanics):
"For the purposes of calculating fees and true-ups, the following sequence shall apply: (1) Aggregate usage will be evaluated against the Fee Band schedule to determine the applicable Band Rate, subject to SKU multipliers set forth in Schedule 1; (2) The Minimum Monthly Commitment (the "Floor") will be applied and any shortfall will be billed as specified; (3) At true-up, credits applied under the Cap provision shall be calculated on net billed tokens after Floor adjustments and shall not result in duplicate credits for the same usage period."

On harmonization: we recommend harmonized bands + SKU multipliers. Commercially the simplest concession is a one-time implementation credit to address the transition (we can think of this as a migration credit). Permanent band changes materially affect long-term ARR and should only be offered with a multi-quarter commit.

Impact estimates (rough):
- One-time migration credit: up to 8-10% of first quarter ARR for the account (flex depending on AOV).
- Permanent band change: ~3-5% reduction in price per token long term; requires 12-month commit to offset.

I've attached proposed_annex_markup.docx for tracking. If everyone signs off, I can send the tracked version to Emma and suggest a 30-minute sync to walk Polaris through the math.

Karthik Iyer
Director, Commercial Strategy — Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com

Attachment: proposed_annex_markup.docx

From: Emma Jones <emma.jones@polarishealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, sofia_ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, procurement@polarishealth.com
Date: 2027-01-19T09:00:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Pricing annex: harmonization ask for fee bands and caps

Thanks Karthik / Sofia — that is very helpful and much clearer. The proposed sequence for true-up calculation looks workable for our legal team; the SKU multiplier approach also answers a lot of our ops concerns.

A couple of small follow-ups before we finalize:
- On the migration credit, would Redwood be comfortable doing a one-time credit applied in the first invoice after execution? We prefer credits on invoice vs. retroactive refunds.
- On the rollback carveout, can we expand "infrastructure events" to explicitly include cloud-region-wide outages and maintenance windows declared by Redwood? We'll accept the 30-day notice but need a short exception for region-wide incidents that may be declared with less notice.

If you can confirm the invoice-credit approach and tweak the rollback language to include region-wide incidents, we can route the tracked annex through our legal and aim to sign next week. Please send the tracked doc and I'll circulate.

Best,
Emma Jones
Sr. Procurement Manager, Polaris Health
